edition.alertText: US strikes IRGC ground control station on Qeshm Island — first attack on the island since June; Iran fires missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain — US and Bahraini defenses intercept; IRGC claims 3 tankers hit mines in Hormuz; tanker struck by 2 projectiles near Oman; Indian-crewed dhow MSV Al Jusufi attacked — 1 Indian seafarer killed, 13 rescued; Brent recovers to $103.89 (+0.28%) after Monday's 7.6% crash; WTI at $95.57 (-0.54%); Rezaei: US response 'not convincing' — deal still out of reach; Qatar: feedback from both sides expected within 36 hours; Trump confirms Qeshm strike on Fox — 'just a minor attack'; Trump announces end to $4B Israel aid by year-end; US midterms underway — polls forecast Democratic takeover; Iran prepares 'maximum deterrence' plan; IRGC updates target lists; Saudi Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B; Aramco begins 'preliminary' East-West pipeline expansion engineering; Saudi coalition intercepts drone over Mecca; Houthis say Saudi strikes killed 17 over 2 days; Iran inflation at 88.7%; gasoline $4.15/gal (AAA)

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis reached day 249 with the US striking Iran's Qeshm Island on the eve of midterm elections — the first attack on the island since a desalination plant strike in June — even as Qatar-mediated peace talks continued in parallel. US officials said the strikes targeted an IRGC ground control station after Iranian forces fired surface-to-air missiles at US assets. CENTCOM reported destroying three one-way attack drones aimed at civilian mariners. In the same exchange, Iran fired several ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain — two missiles aimed at Kuwait fell short or broke apart, while US and Bahraini defenses intercepted three missiles targeting Bahrain. The IRGC framed the exchange as retaliation and claimed it targeted the US Fifth Fleet headquarters, a US air base, and helicopters — all denied by the Pentagon. Trump confirmed the strike on Fox News, calling it 'just a minor attack, it wasn't war,' while adding that a deal with Iran 'could happen.' However, Iran's chief negotiator Mohsen Rezaei called the US response 'not convincing' and said the strait would reopen only if all seven Iranian conditions were met. Qatar said both sides were reviewing a draft proposal and expected feedback within 36 hours. Vice President Vance expressed hope for a 'negotiated settlement' but the Qeshm strike cast doubt on near-term prospects. In a significant development, Trump announced the US would cut off $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel by year-end, reportedly after Netanyahu agreed 'months ago.' Iran's armed forces chief outlined five principles for regional peace, while the IRGC said it was updating its target lists for 'maximum deterrence' — expanding to include US and Israeli assets across wider geographical areas.

Oil markets whipsawed as Monday's 7.6% crash on peace hopes partially reversed after the Qeshm strike. Brent recovered to $103.89 (+0.28%) by Wednesday, remaining down more than 8% for the week, while WTI slipped to $95.57 (-0.54%) — both benchmarks sharply lower than the October 30 peak of $117.64. Gold traded flat at $3,935/oz as safe-haven demand balanced between diplomatic optimism and escalation risk. Newcastle coal eased to $149.50/tonne (-1.94%). US gasoline averaged $4.15/gal (AAA), down marginally from Monday. Saudi Aramco reported Q3 net profit surging 34.6% to $36.3 billion on an average realized price of $95.20/bbl, and its CEO said the company was exploring new export routes with 'preliminary' engineering underway for the East-West pipeline expansion from 7 to 10 million b/d. Breakwave Advisors reported Hormuz flows at approximately 11.7 million b/d in October, up from 9.8 million in September but still below the pre-war baseline of roughly 14.5 million b/d. About 80 VLCCs remain in Gulf-of-Oman shuttle operations with average round voyages of 23 days versus an optimal 9-10 days. VLCC fixtures for Arabian Gulf-China routes ran at $469K/day (Tankers International/Mercuria), with Gulf-Far East at $439K/day (Vitol) — both down significantly from the October peaks but more than double the $200K market-wide average. Gulf-of-Oman loadings avoiding Hormuz transit fetched $220-230K/day. Shipping and logistics now account for roughly 30% of per-barrel costs versus 5% pre-war (ADNOC).

The maritime situation remained volatile despite the diplomatic thaw. A tanker was struck by two projectiles off Oman's northeast coast on November 3, damaging its engine room with no injuries. The Indian-crewed dhow MSV Al Jusufi was attacked, killing one Indian seafarer with 13 crew rescued. Iran's Navy claimed a tanker struck a mine, and the IRGC said three tankers caught fire after hitting mines while transiting 'without permission' — claims unverified by CENTCOM. Iranian state media claimed 11 tankers had caught fire in the strait over nine days. The estimated wartime attack total now stands at approximately 202 incidents. UKMTO confirmed 30+ attacks in October alone — double September and the worst month since the war began. The IRGC also claimed it shot down two Lucas drones over Bandar Khamir. On the Yemen front, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a drone over Mecca and reported another drone destroyed later in the day. The Houthis said Saudi strikes killed 17 people over two days. Houthi ground forces remain within 80 km of Aden. An estimated 350-400 ships remain stranded in the Arabian Gulf, with approximately 490 vessels waiting outside the strait. On Iran's home front, the IRGC said Iran would decide the 'time and conditions' for ending attacks. The country faces 88.7% annual inflation. Iran executed four men on November 3, including two for protest involvement. Lufthansa said its 2026 fuel costs would be €2 billion higher amid the war. The Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia was postponed to December 2027.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for third consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas at €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B.
